title: Congruent triangles
parts: △ABC ≅ △DEF
The triangles have the same shape and size, with A matching D, B matching E, and C matching F.
example: Congruence gives AB=DE and angle B equal to angle E.
note: Letter order identifies the corresponding vertices.
wrong: The triangles have the same shape but may have different sizes.

title: Parallel lines
parts: AB ∥ CD
The line through A and B is parallel to the line through C and D.
example: The lines y=2x and y=2x+3 are distinct and parallel.
note: Parallel lines have the same direction. Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle.
wrong: The lines meet at a right angle.

title: Angle named by three points
parts: ∠ABC
The angle with vertex B and arms through A and C.
example: If A is east of B and C is north of B, the smaller ∠ABC is 90°.
note: The middle letter identifies the vertex.

title: Slope between two points
parts: m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁)
Slope is change in y divided by change in x.
note: A vertical line has undefined slope because its change in x is zero.
wrong: Change in x divided by change in y.

title: Point–slope equation
parts: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)
The line with slope m through (x₁,y₁).
example: A line with slope 2 through (1,3) is y−3=2(x−1).
note: The fixed point (x₁,y₁) is on the line, and (x,y) is a variable point.
wrong: A line through the origin for every x₁ and y₁.

title: Centre and radius of a circle
parts: (x − h)² + (y − k)²
The squared distance from centre (h,k)
= r²
equals the square of the radius.
note: Inside a bracket, y+3 means y−(−3). The radius is √16, not 16.
wrong: A circle with centre (−h,−k) and radius r².

title: Perpendicular distance to a line
parts: d = |ax₀ + by₀ + c|/√(a² + b²)
The shortest distance from (x₀,y₀) to ax+by+c=0.
example: For (3,2) and the line x−1=0, d=|3−1|/1=2.
note: The bars remove the sign, because distance is non-negative.
wrong: The distance from (x₀,y₀) to the origin.

title: Pythagoras’ theorem
parts: a² + b² = c²
In a right triangle the squared legs add to the squared hypotenuse.
note: c labels the side opposite the right angle.
wrong: The leg lengths themselves add to the hypotenuse.

title: Sine in a right triangle
parts: sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse
Divide the side opposite θ by the hypotenuse.
example: An opposite side 3 and hypotenuse 5 give sin θ=3/5.
note: Which side is opposite depends on the angle chosen.
wrong: Divide the adjacent side by the hypotenuse.

title: Cosine in a right triangle
parts: cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse
Divide the leg next to θ by the hypotenuse.
example: An adjacent side 4 and hypotenuse 5 give cos θ=4/5.
note: The adjacent leg is the side next to θ that is not the hypotenuse.
wrong: Divide the opposite side by the hypotenuse.

title: Tangent in a right triangle
parts: tan θ = opposite/adjacent
Divide the opposite leg by the adjacent leg.
example: An opposite leg 3 and adjacent leg 4 give tan θ=3/4.
note: Both numerator and denominator are legs.
wrong: Divide the opposite leg by the hypotenuse.

title: Sine rule
notation: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C
parts: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C
Each side divided by the sine of its opposite angle has the same value.
example: If A=30°, a=4 and B=90°, then b=4×sin 90°/sin 30°=8.
note: Match a lowercase side to its opposite uppercase angle.
wrong: Each side is divided by the sine of its adjacent angle.

title: Cosine rule
parts: c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C
Square the side opposite C using the adjacent sides and their included angle.
example: If a=3, b=4 and C=90°, the cosine term is zero and c=5.
note: C must be the angle between sides a and b.

title: Area of a circular sector
parts: The sector area is the fraction of a full turn times the area of the disc.
example: A 90° sector of radius 4 has area ¼×16π=4π.
note: The denominator 360° applies when θ is measured in degrees.
wrong: Multiply the fraction of the turn by the circumference.

title: Angle in radians
parts: θ = s/r
The angle in radians is arc length divided by radius.
example: A semicircle has arc πr, so the angle is π radians.
note: The ratio s/r gives radians. A semicircle is also 180 degrees.
wrong: Divide radius by arc length to get degrees.

title: Pythagorean trigonometric identity
parts: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1
The squares of sine and cosine at the same angle sum to one.
example: At 30°, the two squared terms are ¼ and ¾.
note: sin² θ means (sin θ)², rather than sin(θ²).
wrong: Take the sine and cosine of θ² and add them.

title: Enlargement scale factor
parts: A′ = k²A
Enlarging lengths by factor k multiplies area by k squared.
example: A triangle of area 5 enlarged by factor 3 has area 45.
note: Area scales by k² even though length scales by k.
wrong: Multiply the area by k only.
